elements.element: Audit frequency limited to no more than once per 12 months

elements.evidence: "Each audit shall be conducted during business hours"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations"

elements.element: Vendor bears audit cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "may not remotely access Customer's systems and records"; "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly"

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent" (stricter, customer-favourable)

reasons: All six preferred atomic elements are present: 12-month frequency cap, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent confidentiality-bound auditor, Vendor-borne cost subject to the 5% underpayment trigger, and an express prohibition on direct/remote system access.

The pre-existing cost-allocation and access-carve-out language in 22.2 was left untouched, so unrelated commercial terms and the 5% threshold remain effective; converting the remote-access grant into a prohibition removes the contradiction with 22.2.

Minimality fails only narrowly: "off-site where possible" adds a location restriction that the preferred position does not require and that duplicates the no-direct-access protection already secured in 22.1 and 22.2. Deleting that phrase would make the edit fully minimal.
No undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced; the inserted sentence uses defined parties and existing concepts.
